items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to tickets purchased for use on the Long Island Rail Road
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3778

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the public authorities law, in relation to tickets purchased
for use on the Long Island Rail Road

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
To eliminate the cost of mandated
surcharges for the cancellation of Long Island Rail Road tickets
within six months of their original purchase.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
Section 1205 of the public authorities
law is amended by adding subdivision 9; requiring the Metropolitan
Transit Authority to reimburse one hundred percent (100%) of the
purchase price for unused Long Island Rail Road tickets returned
within six months of the date of purchase and prohibiting the
assessment of any surcharge or processing fee for the returned ticket.

JUSTIFICATION:
On December 30, 2010, the Metropolitan Transit
Authority (MTA) Board adopted a new refund policy for tickets
purchased for the Long Island Rail Road (LIRR). The recently
instituted policy invalidates Unused One Way and Round Trip tickets
within two weeks of the purchase date. For a full refund, any unused
tickets must be returned within 30 days of the purchase date. Prior
to this policy's enactment, LIRR tickets had been valid for up to
sixth months.

In addition to the reduction in the amount of time allowed for
full-refund ticket returns, the new policy also includes a $10 refund
processing fee for each ticket return transaction. In most cases, the
$10 processing fee is more than the cost of the purchased One-Way
ticket. This policy discourages transit riders from obtaining a
refund, losing the cost of the ticket if they are unable use the
ticket within 14 days.

This legislation will eliminate the inequitable charge of the $10
processing fee for refunded tickets and prolong the use of tickets
for a reasonable amount of time.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
Unknown.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the thirtieth day
after it shall have become a law.
